DILG BAGONG Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA cor. Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City www.dil . ov. h OILG OPINION NO. MAY 15 2025 ANGELINA DINGLASAN Authorized Lotto Agent Philippine Charity Sweepstakes Office Geedinglasan41@qmail.com Dear Ms. Dinglasan: This has reference to your electronic mail dated March 26, 2025, concerning DILG Legal Opinion No. 83, Series of 2024. In particular, you are requesting that this Department issue a memorandum circular, as the aforesaid legal opinion is ostensibly not being accorded due consideration by the local government units (LGUs). To recall, on March 19, 2024, this Department received your email seeking assistance regarding the alleged continued insistence of LGUs that authorized lotto agents secure a mayor's permit despite the discussions during the Senate hearings held on January 25 and February 1 , 2024, where Senators Rafael Tulfo and Koko Pimentel emphasized that LGUs should recognize the exemptions provided under Section 4 of Republic Act (RA) No. 1169, as amended, and Presidential Decree (PD) No. 771. At the outset, may we note that legal opinions are fundamentally dynamic and may evolve based on more comprehensive legal analysis. Having said that, upon further perusal, this Department finds LGUs retain regulatory authority, such as the imposition of a mayor's permit notwithstanding the business tax exemption of Lotto Agents. Accordingly, this Department of the submission that LGUs may legally require Lotto Agents to obtain a business permit or mayor's permit as a condition precedent to operate within their respective jurisdictions. While Lotto Agents may be exempt from the imposition of local business taxes pursuant to RA 1169, as amended by PD 771, such exemption does not extend to regulatory measures. As such, LGUs are not precluded from requiring Lotto Agents to obtain a mayor's permit. In DILG Legal Opinion No. 144, Series of 2022, we opined, citing Section 152(c) of the Republic Act No. 71601 , or the Local Government Code (hereinafter referred to as "Section 152. Xxx (c) Barangay Clearance. - No city or municipality may issue any license or permit for qnv business or activitv unless a "Matino, Mahusay at Maaasahan" Trunkline No.: 8876-34-54

the Code), that a mayor's permit is a regulatory measure exercised by the city/municipality pursuant to the delegated police power given by the Congress to the LGUs. A mayor's permit is issued as an exercise of delegated police power in relation to the promotion of the general welfare of the people in the LGUs. Accordingly, the objective of such a permit is to ensure that activities or businesses comply with existing laws and other regulatory requirements necessary for the maintenance of order and general welfare within the locality. To bolster this, the Supreme Court, in Philippines, Inc. v. Bases Conversion Development Authority,2 distinguishes between the power to tax and the power to regulate. The Court elucidated that the power to regulate is an exercise of police power. Premised on the foregoing, this Department opines that LGUs are well within their power to require Lotto Agents to obtain a mayor's permit within their jurisdiction. This opinion is being rendered without prejudice to any contrary opinion of competent authorities or the courts. We hope to have guided you on the matter. Thank you. Very truly yours, BY AUTHORITY OF THE SECRETARY . ROMEO P. BENITEZ Undersecretary for External, Legal and Legislative Affairs OUSELLA'RPB/LLLs-LRALLD/jam ARIEL O.
